clue.text: Representatives requiring a toilet

parts.note: taken as written
the Gents is the British name for a men's public lavatory

explanation.surface: Delegates on a trip urgently needing to find a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gents is everyday British for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: People who act on behalf of others, such as sales or estate representatives, are called by this name.

clue.text: A job with the French follower of Jesus

parts.note: taken as written
a post is a job or position
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French position offered to one of Christ's disciples.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the twelve chosen disciples sent out to spread Christ's teaching is given this title.

clue.text: Sussex travel agent wants some more

indicators.note: wants some means we need only a portion of the phrase before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the county and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A travel agent on England's south coast is greedy for more business.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county in southern England; 'agent' is just scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional beyond the usual amount is an addition, an adjective meaning more.

clue.text: Huge vessel could be in attic

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big pot or ship model might be stored in the loft.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous ocean liner that sank in 1912 was a giant ship, and the word also means enormous.

clue.text: Cowardly shout and cry of pain

parts.note: to shout loudly is to yell
the exclamation people make when hurt

explanation.surface: A frightened person shouting and crying out when hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone lacking courage is said to have a streak of this colour, so the adjective means timid.

clue.text: Come out of gate finally and mix

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of gate
to merge is to blend together

explanation.surface: Crowds leave a stadium gate at last and mingle together.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or become visible after being hidden is a synonym for coming out.

clue.text: Bit of fun with football team's bloomers?

parts.note: a lark is a prank or bit of fun
Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: A prank involving footballers' baggy knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers suggests old-fashioned underwear or blunders, but here means plants that bloom; Spurs is the London club Tottenham Hotspur.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphiniums with spurred flowers are garden plants, and anything that blooms is cheekily called a bloomer.

clue.text: Saturday and Sunday Ken goes in to tend garden

indicators.note: goes in means the named man is placed inside another word

parts.note: to weed is to clear a garden of unwanted plants
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ken spends his days off doing the gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: The two days at the end of the working week, when many people rest, together form this period.

clue.text: Wrongly portrays miser going out to get gifts

indicators.note: going out suggests being thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
presents are gifts

explanation.surface: A stingy man is unfairly described as going shopping for gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a false or misleading account of someone is to depict them inaccurately, a present tense verb.

clue.text: Announce appointment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put up a notice publicly
second meaning: a job or position someone is given

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like publicising a booking, but the two words are separate senses: a verb for publishing and a noun for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: One may publish news by putting it on a noticeboard, and a position held in an organisation is also called this.

clue.text: Title Rosie worked out for bathroom things

indicators.note: something worked out has been rearranged and solved, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Rosie devising a heading for a list of bathroom items.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap, shampoo, toothpaste and similar washing products kept by the basin are collectively known by this word.

clue.text: Street water filter

parts.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A device for cleaning the water supply in a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass liquid through a sieve or mesh to remove solids is a common kitchen verb meaning to filter.

clue.text: Reg tries changing record

indicators.note: changing the order of letters produces a new arrangement of the words before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Reg attempts to switch his gramophone disc.
explanation.definitionFit: An official list or log, such as a school attendance roll, is a written record of names or events.

clue.text: Viewer often seen standing on the promenade?

definitions.text: Viewer often seen standing on the promenade?

parts.words: Viewer often seen standing on the promenade?
parts.note: surface reading: a sightseer who stands about on the seafront

parts.words: Viewer often seen standing on the promenade?
parts.note: setter's reading: the viewer is an instrument on a stand, coin-operated on many seaside piers

explanation.walkthrough: A viewer sounds like a person, but here it is a device for looking through, mounted on the seafront for tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: British seaside towns place coin-operated magnifying optical instruments along the seafront so visitors can look out to sea.

clue.text: Bride hung around somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: around suggests moving things about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bride lingered somewhere north of the border for her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Scotland is a specific location there, so 'somewhere' covers it as an example.

clue.text: Regretted sounding rude

indicators.note: sounding tells us to go by how the next word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: the word for impolite is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for having come across as impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sorrow or remorse over something done is to repent of it, a past tense verb here.

clue.text: Spoke of one in unhappy surroundings

indicators.note: one item placed in surroundings goes inside the other word
surroundings are what encloses something, so this word forms the outer shell

parts.note: unhappy is sad, here forming the outside
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Talking about a person living in miserable conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tenses of verbs meaning to utter words aloud in speech or remark.

clue.text: Frightens about five, putting these round their necks?

definitions.note: a description of a plural noun: things people wear

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: to scare is to frighten
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A gang menaces five people by wrapping something round their throats.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of woollen or silk cloth worn wrapped about the throat for warmth are what people put there.

clue.text: Oral examinations are required for this job

definitions.text: Oral examinations are required for this job

parts.note: surface reading: spoken tests, as in a language exam
setter's reading: inspections of the mouth and teeth

explanation.walkthrough: Oral exams suggests passing spoken tests to qualify; read literally, it is examining mouths as daily work.
explanation.definitionFit: The profession of caring for teeth and gums involves checking patients' mouths, making it a fitting name for the job.

clue.text: A down-trodden machine operator

parts.note: surface reading: an oppressed factory worker
setter's reading: a part pressed down by the foot that drives a machine

explanation.walkthrough: Down-trodden suggests a downtrodden worker; read literally it is something trodden downward to make a machine go.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-pumped lever that powers a sewing machine or lathe is literally pushed down by the feet and operates it.

clue.text: About to get weary, so withdrew

parts.note: re means about or concerning
weary means tired

explanation.surface: Someone, nearly exhausted, gave up and left.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place or go to bed, or to stop working, all fit the past tense verb meaning withdrew.

clue.text: Shout in terror: "Second best!"

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: Someone yells in horror at only coming runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud high-pitched cry of fear or pain is what someone gives out when terrified.

clue.text: Hairdresser endlessly needing reminder of meal outside

indicators.note: endlessly means without its last letter, so the word for hairdresser is cut short

parts.note: a men's hairdresser
a cue is a prompt to an actor

explanation.surface: A forgetful hairdresser needs prompting about an outdoor meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where food is grilled over charcoal in the garden is an outdoor meal of this kind.

clue.text: It's sex that's ruined lives

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moralising complaint that sexual affairs have wrecked people's lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb: is alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive or to have being in the world is to have existence, a present tense verb matching this one.

clue.text: Put down as late

parts.note: surface reading: recording someone as tardy in a register
setter's reading: to lay in the ground one who is deceased

explanation.walkthrough: Late usually means tardy, but here it means dead, and putting the dead down is burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a corpse in a grave is a formal verb for laying the deceased to rest.

clue.text: Too hot when finished, he'd eat inside

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: inside tells us one word is to be placed within another

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man felt overheated once he had finished eating indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heated past its proper temperature, such as an engine, is described this way.

clue.text: Sour, yet it could be sweet!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sharp or acid in taste

definitions.note: a description of a noun: a sweet pastry is one example
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pastry case with a filling, often a dessert

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sets two opposite tastes against each other; the same word is a sharp flavour and a pastry dish, often a sweet one.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means acidic in flavour; as a noun it is a baked pastry dish, such as a jam or lemon one.

clue.text: Seem upset about central heating plan

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is wrapped around the other
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for central heating, used in property adverts

explanation.surface: Someone appears unhappy about a proposed heating installation plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic arrangement or programme of action, like a pension or savings one, is a synonym for plan.

clue.text: Are in colour when brought up

indicators.note: in means the first word is placed within the second

parts.note: red is a colour, forming the outside
taken as written

explanation.surface: Children blush when someone mentions their upbringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising children or animals until grown is to bring them up, a past participle matching this one.
